newsitem.title: USA: Analysts cut Claire's EPS, cite weak sales.
newsitem.headline: Analysts cut Claire's EPS, cite weak sales.

text.p: PaineWebber and Raymond James on Monday cut their fiscal year earnings estimates for Claire's Stores Inc, citing weak sales.
Raymond James analyst Harry Katica said the retailer's lower-than-expected holiday sales prompted him to cut its earnings to $0.90 from $0.99 for the fiscal year ending in January 1997.
He said he cut the company's EPS for the following fiscal year to $1.05 from $1.18
"If they didn't meet their expectations in the strongest week of the year, it's an uphil battle to do it in the rest of the year," Katica said.
Claire's shares fell 2-3/4 to 11-3/4 Monday afternoon.
PaineWebber analyst Stephanie Giroux said she cut the company's earnings for the current fiscal year to $0.93 and lowered the following year's earnings to $1.12.
